clue.text: Something tasty one's fed to doctor

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: MO is short for medical officer, a doctor
one is I, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A treat is being spoon-fed to a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a savoury Japanese fermented soybean paste, a flavoursome food used in soups.

clue.text: Frenchman Lehár trained as composer

indicators.note: something trained is reshaped and directed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is Monsieur, the French title for a man
the name taken as written, without its accent

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and the operetta writer Franz Lehár both study to become composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lehár, the composer of The Merry Widow, is fodder here, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian late-Romantic composer, famous for his large symphonies.

clue.text: Top criminal seizing power

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so the criminal word wraps around the letter for power

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A leading crook takes control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective for the boss criminal, but it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is a toy that spins on its point, so it can be called a spinner.

clue.text: How Buñuel may have interpreted White House film?

parts.words: How Buñuel may have interpreted White House
parts.note: Luis Buñuel was a Spanish film director, and the clue asks how a Spanish speaker would put 'white house' into his own language
the result is the title of the 1942 Bogart and Bergman wartime classic

explanation.surface: A famous director reimagines the US presidential residence as cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish casa means house and blanca means white; the Moroccan city named this way gave its name to the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is the celebrated 1942 Hollywood movie starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Hunter in exploit over enormously long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: an act is a deed or exploit
an aeon is an immeasurably long age

explanation.surface: A hunter performs a feat lasting an extremely long time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon was a huntsman turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: High-flyers must have raw rice boiled

indicators.note: boiling churns things about in the pot, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ambitious achievers insist their uncooked rice be boiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyers' suggests ambitious people, but literally means those who fly an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the team who operate a plane, people who literally fly high.

clue.text: Keep away from bore — don't get involved

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: do not go near a bore, a drilled shaft for water
second meaning: the idiom for not meddling in a situation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' seems to be a tedious person, but it is a borehole, so the phrase can be read word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means refrain from interfering with something that is fine as it is.

clue.text: Darkness is terrible thing

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the following word's letters are mangled

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy pronouncement that darkness is something awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period between dusk and dawn when there is no daylight.

clue.text: Aussie river rising in impressive display

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going upwards, so the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Yarra flows through Melbourne, Australia

explanation.surface: An Australian river in flood makes a spectacular sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' sounds like a river in spate, but it turns the name upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive range or arrangement of things laid out for show.

clue.text: Conflicting positions?

parts.note: surface reading: opinions or stances that contradict each other
setter's reading: the places crew members take up for conflict, when a ship prepares for battle

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the command for troops or sailors to take their posts ready for combat.

clue.text: Means to reduce capital growth?

parts.note: surface reading: a financial measure that shrinks the growth of invested capital, and in finance this word names a cut in an asset's value
setter's reading: capital is the head, and its growth is what sprouts on it

explanation.surface: An economist proposes a measure to rein in investment returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim removes what grows on top of the head; bankers also use the word for a reduction in asset value.

clue.text: Substantial domestic plot — study extracted mineral

parts.note: substantial things are real, actually existing

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, so the word for study is taken away from the plot

parts.note: the plot of land beside a house
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a large garden from which the study has been removed, leaving a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Realgar is an orange-red arsenic sulphide ore, used historically as a pigment.

clue.text: Weariness seen in pupil regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these three words

explanation.surface: A teacher notices a pupil keeps looking tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless boredom and lack of interest, a mental tiredness.

clue.text: Seriously old walls in home

indicators.note: to wall something in is to surround it, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: early in the sense of from a former time
a bird's home, or any cosy dwelling

explanation.surface: Seriously, the old house is surrounded by walls.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLY surrounds NEST: EAR-NEST-LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe acting with sincere, grave intent rather than lightly or in jest.

clue.text: Tree line to extend over

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to arch is to curve or span over something

explanation.surface: A row of trees stretches over a path.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer that sheds its needles each autumn.

clue.text: Virgin and Pole drowned in beer

indicators.note: something drowned in liquid is fully submerged inside it, so these pieces go within the drink

parts.note: a brew is a beer, or any brewed drink
taken as written
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A teetotal visitor and a Polish friend end up sozzled in beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' and 'Pole' both look like people in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin can mean untouched or unused, as in virgin snow, so something entirely new.

clue.text: Star appearing in many westerns

parts.note: surface reading: a lead actor who features in many cowboy films
setter's reading: the star-shaped emblem pinned to a sheriff's chest

explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff's tin star is the insignia of office worn on the shirt, a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Erstwhile partner works to return bonus

parts.note: a former spouse or lover is an ex

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word for works is read backwards

parts.note: works of art, collectively art

explanation.surface: A former spouse comes back to work for a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: EX then ART backwards (TRA).
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something additional on top of what is expected, like a perk.

clue.text: Mature blue

definitions.meaning: second meaning: sexually explicit, as in a blue film

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour or a mood; here it is the sense of risqué content.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means grown-up, and is also the euphemism for explicit material meant for over-eighteens.

clue.text: Tomb, cold, seen by Pound coming into Italian city church

indicators.note: seen by means set beside, so the pieces simply sit next to each other

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: coming into a place means entering it, so this piece goes inside the city

parts.note: Italy's capital
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A traveller notes a chilly tomb, a church, and the poet Ezra Pound visiting an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like the American poet who lived in Italy, but it is the currency sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromlech is a prehistoric megalithic burial chamber, a dolmen of standing stones.

clue.text: Rent increased? Go to pieces

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split, a crack
a price that has increased has gone up

explanation.surface: A tenant faced with a rent rise falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a split.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is to break down mentally or emotionally, collapsing under strain.

clue.text: Red, green, blue or black card?

parts.words: Red, green, blue or black card?
parts.note: surface reading: a coloured playing card or penalty card
setter's reading: these are colours of snooker balls, but a 'card' is an eccentric person, and only a strange kind of ball would be one

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a card is a comic, eccentric character; red, green, blue and black are ball colours in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or peculiar person, a real character, is called a card in British slang.

clue.text: Watertight chamber is thus enclosed in metal

indicators.note: something enclosed in a casing sits inside it, so the phrase goes within the metal

parts.note: a can is a metal tin
is, plus so meaning thus

explanation.surface: An engineer notes a sealed chamber is encased in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: CA + IS SO + N.
explanation.definitionFit: A caisson is a sealed underwater chamber in which construction work is done below water level.

clue.text: Guard against black sheep eating a rook

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so the sheep surrounds the two letters

parts.note: B for black, as on pencils
a ewe is a female sheep
taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A farmer protects against the black sheep of the flock eating a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: B + EW(AR)E. 'Black sheep' reads as a phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To beware of something is to be cautious and on the lookout to protect oneself from it.

clue.text: Catch tense boy round north in important region

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the boy goes around the compass point

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a lad is a boy
N for north

explanation.surface: A nervous boy is caught heading north in an important area.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAR + T + LA(N)D.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartland is the central, most vital area of a country or of support for a cause.

clue.text: Bird initially near atomic plant

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the next two words are used

parts.note: first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A bird starts out close to a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atomic plant' reads as a power station, but plant is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a shrub whose leaves yield a reddish dye used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Vessel and wine, unopened, brought into sober meeting

indicators.note: brought into a gathering means placed inside it

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose meetings are for staying sober

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, so the wine loses its first letter

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: An unopened bottle of wine is carried into a temperance meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a bottle; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood out of the heart, the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Get wisdom about current in French river

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for wisdom surrounds the electrical symbol

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge and wisdom
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone seeks wisdom about the current in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: LORE surrounds I: LO(I)RE. 'Current' suits a river in the surface, but it is the symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic.

clue.text: King visiting apparently empty county?

indicators.note: someone visiting is staying inside a place for a while, so the king goes within the next phrase

parts.note: a place that seems empty has no folk, no people in it
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch tours a county that seems deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into NO FOLK: NO(R)FOLK. Norfolk is a rural county in eastern England, often joked about as sparsely populated, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is an English county on the East Anglian coast, here defined by an example.

clue.text: Is a name recollected? Not with this!

definitions.text: Is a name recollected? Not with this!

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: can you remember a name with this condition? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: 'recollected' means remembered on the surface and re-collected for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so with it a person cannot recall names or anything else.

clue.text: Water to swallow very quietly in throat part

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the water phrase surrounds the music marking

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jokey old British term for water, the only drink Adam had
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone gulps water very softly down their throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old joking name for water, since Adam had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the visible bulge of the larynx cartilage at the front of the neck.

clue.text: Some work needed in joint

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a portion of them is used

parts.note: the end of work and the start of needed

explanation.surface: A surgeon says a joint requires some repair.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and shin, a major leg articulation.
